newsitem.title: UK: British Telecom extends gains in busy trade.
newsitem.headline: British Telecom extends gains in busy trade.

text.p: UK telecommunications giant British Telecom Plc (BT), a key member of London's FTSE 100 index of leading companies, on Thursday saw its share price pushed up through support levels in heavy trading.
By 1535 GMT BT stock was up 14p at 400-1/2p as trading volume topped 25 million shares. It was the second most active FTSE stock.

Analysts said a mixture of driving forces were creating the bullish sentiment. News late on Wednesday that chief executive Sir Peter Bonfield was to acquire around 130,000 BT shares under a renumeration package was helping the stock, traders said.
"That's one hell of a vote of confidence," said John Tysoe of SocGen, "and with good reason."
He said BT was also attracting buyers because its stock price was considerably cheaper than sector rivals.
Industry analysts said a lot of arbitrage business had taken place in MCI and BT ahead of the planned merger of the two firms.
Their merger application was filed to the US Federal Communications Committee (FCC) on Tuesday for approval.
"It's basically a technical situation which has exacerbated things today," said one analyst.
Most traders thought Wednesday's report that Cellnet -- of which BT owns 60 percent -- planned to invest one billion stg over five years had a negligible effect on BT shares.
Big programme trades and heavy option activity also helped the shares, analysts said.
